text: Everis has a different standard for talent. We do not use years of experience, titles, or pedigree as substitutes for ability. We look for exceptional work, sound judgment, fast learning, ownership, and evidence of impact. It is not a lower bar. It is a sharper one. We’re looking for an accomplished software engineer who has built real mobile applications and already has practical exposure to growth, experimentation, conversion optimization, or broader product work. This role requires both engineering depth and evidence that you can think beyond implementation. Join Everis at a defining stage of growth. Help shape the product, influence the company we become, and grow with us. Work 100% remotely from anywhere, benefit from unlimited leave, and connect with colleagues at company-sponsored international retreats in some of the world’s most inspiring cities. About Everis Everis is a growing, remote-first software company founded by proven technology entrepreneurs Rob Rawson and Liam Martin, who previously built Time Doctor into an eight-figure global SaaS business. We acquire promising mobile apps and SaaS companies, invest in their future, and improve their products, technology, and customer experience. Our ambition is to make Everis the best long-term home for exceptional software products—and a company where exceptional people can take real ownership, do consequential work, and grow with us. About the Product Pebble is Everis ’s growing, speaking-first language-learning app for iOS and Android. It helps people learn English, Spanish, and French through practical lessons, pronunciation practice, and guided conversations that get them speaking from day one. The product is live and evolving quickly, with major opportunities across onboarding, habit formation, activation, retention, conversion, and new markets. Your engineering and product decisions will directly influence how well people learn and how quickly Pebble grows. What makes this role different Most engineering roles begin after the problem, solution, and ticket have already been defined. Here, you join the work earlier. You will remain a software engineer first, but you will also identify product problems, decide what to test, build the solution, measure the outcome, and use the evidence to determine what happens next. This is not a marketing role for someone who codes; it is an engineering role with responsibility for product outcomes. What you’ll work on Build, ship, and improve Pebble’s mobile applications. Find friction across onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, conversion, and monetization. Turn product questions into improvements, prototypes, A/B tests, and other useful experiments. Use product and user data to understand behavior and decide what should be built next. Define success measures, analyze results, and act on what you learn. Work directly with our founders and product and business leadership. Balance strong engineering with the speed required to test ideas and learn. What you need to bring This is a mobile engineering job first. You need to have built, shipped, and supported a production mobile app. We mean a real product used by real people - not just a demo or code sample. We also need proof you've thought beyond implementation. Show us at least one of these: Breadth beyond implementation. Direct mobile-growth or conversion work You must show meaningful evidence of at least one of the following: growth experimentation, A/B or split testing, conversion optimization, product ownership, building and operating your own software product. Conversion optimization. You improved a real flow: onboarding, activation, a paywall, trial-to-paid, checkout, or another point where users dropped. Core Stack. Strong engineering fundamentals and sound judgment about reliability, maintainability, quality, and speed. Flutter/Dart, TypeScript/NestJS, MongoDB, or close equivalents; and App Store or Google Play subscriptions, paywalls, payments, or trial-to-paid journeys. Production mobile engineering. Demonstrated success building and shipping production mobile applications using iOS, Android, cross-platform, or another credible mobile environment. Product development or ownership. You helped decide what to build and why. You didn't just receive a finished specification. You can independently take production software from problem through implementation, release, and iteration. Product-management-type work. You framed the problem, made trade-offs, defined success, or used evidence to choose the next move. A product of your own. You built it, launched it, watched real people use it, and changed it based on what you learned. What good looks like Your fundamentals are solid. APIs, data modelling, testing, debugging, release practices, and production monitoring aren't someone else's job. You can tell the whole story. What was wrong, what you personally built, what happened, and what you did next. You cross boundaries when the problem demands it. Mobile, backend, web, data, analytics - you don't stop at the edge of your code. You'd rather find out than argue from theory. You form a view, test it, and change your mind when the evidence says you should. What we offer Compensation: $80,000–$120,000 USD annually, depending on experience. Consequential ownership: your decisions will directly affect Pebble and Everis . Direct founder access: work closely with experienced entrepreneurs on important product and company decisions. Exceptional colleagues: work with capable, curious, high-ownership people held to the same demanding standard. Room to grow: take on larger problems and greater responsibility as Everis expands. 100% remote: work from anywhere. Unlimited leave: take meaningful time away when you need it. Paid international company trips: come together with the team in some of the world’s most inspiring cities—to collaborate, build lasting relationships, and experience somewhere new. Our recruiting process We keep our process structured and transparent: Initial review: Application → Written Assessment Skills and reasoning: Recorded Scenario Assessment → Reasoning Intelligence Test → Recorded Role-Specific Assessment Interviews: Technical Interview → Final Interview with a Co-Founder Final evaluation: Paid Work Trial If you are an exceptional mobile engineer who wants to help decide what gets built, prove whether it works, and shape a growing product, we want to hear from you. Compensation Range: $80K - $120K Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (100% Remote)
text: the basics We are looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer (m/f/d) to join us as the embedded technical expert who takes our customers from "interested in AI" to running real agentic workflows in production. This is a hands-on, code-shipping role, not an advisory one. You'll work directly inside a customer's environment - understanding their domain, their data, and the business outcomes that matter to them - and build the agentic use cases (using MCPs, skills, and our agent platform) that make those outcomes real. You'll also bring a working understanding of Kubernetes, since our platform is built and operated on it, but that's the foundation you stand on, not the focus of the role. Giant Swarm is a fast-growing open-source infrastructure management platform used by modern enterprises. Our vision is to empower developers around the world to ship great products - this role is core to how we do that with our agent platform. your job You partner directly with a customer as their embedded expert - not just advising, but designing, building, and shipping working agentic solutions in their environment. You get up to speed on a new customer's domain quickly (e.g. smart manufacturing, financial services, whatever it is) and identify the business outcomes AI/agentic workflows can realistically deliver for them. You design and build proof-of-concepts and production-track agentic workflows using MCPs, skills, and our agent platform, tailored to that customer's data and systems. You act as the customer-side expert on what our agent platform can do - translating platform capability into something their engineers can actually use and extend. You work closely with customer engineering teams - some devrel-style enablement, workshops, and pairing so they can own what you build after you move on. You feed the patterns and gaps you find back to the product team, shaping what we build next. You may support pre-sales conversations - helping scope what AI use cases would deliver value for a prospect, and building examples that help make the case for choosing Giant Swarm . requirements You have practical, hands-on experience in a customer-facing technical role (Solutions Architect, Forward Deployed Engineer, or similar). You have real, hands-on experience building with agentic AI - MCPs, agent frameworks, tool-using LLMs, or similar. This is non-negotiable. You can get productive in an unfamiliar business domain fast, and turn what you learn into concrete technical solutions. You have at least a solid working understanding of Kubernetes and cloud-native operations. You communicate clearly and confidently with both customer stakeholders and engineers - this role lives at that interface. Experience with developer relations, workshops, or technical enablement is a strong plus, as is prior Solutions Architect experience. You're comfortable with ambiguity - this is our first hire fully dedicated to agentic customer work, so a lot of the "how" is still being defined as you go. You are able to comfortably align parts of your workday with Europe (UTC +/- 2 hours). salary information We’re a fully remote company and use a formula-based salary calculator to determine starting salaries, factoring in location, experience, and responsibility. This approach helps us avoid pay gaps (e.g., gender pay gap) by basing compensation on objective criteria rather than negotiation. Because we apply a location factor, the actual figure for hires outside Cologne will differ from the reference range above, and the total package may include components beyond base salary (e.g., equity, benefits). We’re publishing this range to comply with the EU Pay Transparency Directive. Your recruiter will walk you through how the calculator applies to your location and level. text: Who we are MixRank processes petabytes of data every month from web crawling. We have hundreds of customers using our data products including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Security. Our team is 50+ full-time, full-remote from 20+ countries. We're growing, profitable, employee-owned, no dependence on outside funding. Applicants from all geographies and backgrounds are welcome. We are looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job but it’s something they love to do. We're obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team. Our code base is very friendly to new contributors. You'll have a fully-functional development environment within hours (fully automated) and be pushing commits on your first day. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in less than 2 minutes. Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, Javascript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you'll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git. We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We operate two datacenters with high performance servers we've built that are capable of dealing with the volumes of data we process. We've implemented our own distributed file system. We do full-scale web crawls. We download and perform static analysis on the entire universe of Android APKs and iOS IPAs that are published. Unlike a typical startup where you'll spend half of your time in meetings, and the other half fixing bugs from Jira tickets— at MixRank you'll get to challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that will help you to grow as an individual. Who we’re looking for We're looking for remote junior engineers that have 0-3 years of professional experience in software, and 5+ years of curiosity exploring computers, programming, and technical hobby projects. title: Software Development Engineer II - Conversations
text: About HighLevel : HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes. To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently. Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability. Our people With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home. Our impact Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that. Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts What are we hiring for? The systems that run millions of businesses. Every month, 2.6 billion messages flow through our platform. Our automation engine enrolls 3.1 billion contacts and executes 21.5 billion workflow actions in the same window - with API traffic peaking at 28,000+ requests per second. If these systems lag, businesses lose leads. If they go down, people lose income. You haven't built at this scale yet. That's fine - almost nobody has. What we're hiring for is the engineer who reads those numbers and feels pulled toward them. Who wants to know what a queue looks like when it's absorbing a 10x burst, what an index does at 1.5 TB, what "eventually consistent" actually means when a customer is staring at the screen. You'll work on real production paths from week one — with senior engineers around you who've broken and fixed these systems before. You'll build. You'll break things. You'll learn faster here than anywhere else. Team & System Overview: The Conversations organization powers multi-channel communication across SMS, Email, WhatsApp, and DMs — handling over 2B messages each month. The Threads & Composer team owns the inbox and composer surfaces, and the backend services that deliver and store those interactions.You’ll work across Node.js microservices, GCP-based infra (GKE, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks), and MongoDB/Firestore storage layers, ensuring every message and UI state stays consistent, fast, and recoverable. Responsibilities: Build and ship features in Node.js / Go services that sit on real production paths — your code handles live traffic, not toy problems Own well-scoped services and components end to end: code, tests, rollout, and monitoring Work with SQL and NoSQL data stores — writing queries, adding indexes, and learning why the schema looks the way it does Get hands-on with queues, caches, and rate limiters — the building blocks of every system here Ship Vue 3 UIs that consume your own APIs — clean components, sane state management, and realtime updates that don't flicker or drift Write design docs for your features and defend them in review — clear thinking, honest trade-offs Join the on-call rotation with backup from senior engineers — incidents are where the deepest learning happens Ask questions relentlessly, absorb feedback from code reviews, and level up fast Requirements: 2+ years of backend engineering experience with strong fundamentals in Node.js, Go, or a comparable language — and the drive to go deep in ours Working knowledge of queues or async processing — you've used Pub/Sub, Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar, and want to master delivery semantics, ordering, and backpressure Genuine interest in distributed systems — you understand the basics (idempotency, retries, consistency trade-offs) and are hungry to learn the rest by building Hands-on with Redis or another cache/in-memory store , even at small scale Comfortable with SQL or NoSQL databases — you can model data, write efficient queries, and reason about indexes Proficient in Vue 3 or a similar modern frontend framework — solid component design and real experience with state management (Pinia, Vuex, or equivalent) You write tests as a habit and can put your design thinking into a clear doc AI-native builder — you code with agents daily and are pushing to get accurate, production-quality output from them Technical Environment: Languages : Node.js (TypeScript), Go Frontend : Vue 3, TypeScript, Pinia, Vite, Tailwind Storage : MongoDB, Firestore, Redis, ElasticSearch, ClickHouse Infra : GCP — GKE, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks CI/CD : GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes Why This Role Most engineers spend years at companies where "scale" means a few hundred requests per second — and never find out what they're capable of. Here, the systems are the teacher. Every design decision has a visible consequence at billions of events a month. Every incident is a masterclass. You'll sit in architecture reviews with staff engineers debating storage engines and consistency models — and within a year, you'll be contributing to those debates, not just watching them. If you optimize your career for learning velocity, there is no faster track than this. On AI We're past the debate. AI is part of how we build - and we expect you to be hungry for it . You already code with agents daily. You're learning what they're good at, where they hallucinate, and how to get accurate, tested, slop-free code out of them fast. You treat AI as a multiplier on your learning speed, not a substitute for understanding. If you're still copy-pasting from a chat window and hoping, this isn't the seat for you. What you're built for You're deeply curious — you don't stop at "it works," you need to know why it works You read post-mortems and system-design write-ups for fun , not because someone assigned them You've built things beyond your job description — side projects, internal tools, that one system you rewrote because the old one bothered you You take feedback like a gift: code review comments make your next PR better, every time When something breaks, your first instinct is curiosity, not panic What Success looks like You own a service or component that the team trusts you on completely You're a dependable on-call engineer — you've debugged real incidents and shipped the fixes Your design docs have gone from "reviewed heavily" to "approved with nits" Senior engineers pull you into harder problems — because you've earned it You're visibly on the path to SDE-3, and everyone around you knows it Bonus Points Familiarity with our stack: GCP, MongoDB, Firestore, ClickHouse, ElasticSearch You've contributed to a messaging, automation, or event-driven system — at any scale Side projects or open-source work that shows you build because you can't not build EEO Statement: The company is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
